The Building Blocks of the Moving Shares

Source: R/jfp_move.R
jfp_dir.Rd

jfp_dir() carries a direction over the joint vector with the movement of every predictor along it. jfp_mv_J() returns the derivative of the expected information of the block's equation, with the predictor indices fixed, along the directions R. jfp_mv_e2() returns the second derivative of every predictor along the two directions. jfp_mv_W() and jfp_mv_Wk() return the whitened derivatives of the block's rows along R, the second one also in each coefficient of the term that holds the block. jfp_mv_etak() returns the derivative of a moving term's block along R; jfp_mv_etakk() its derivative in two of the term's coefficients along R, contracted against per-observation weights; jfp_mv_cv() the derivative of the block's rows in two coefficients of its term along R, contracted against weights on the block's columns. jfp_mv_pfun() wraps a product of two factors with a memory, and jfp_nonempty() lists the non-empty subsets of at most two directions. In a model with a filter, jfp_mv_setpair() selects the ordered pair of equations whose information and rows the other functions read, jfp_mv_full() places directions over the filter's full width, jfp_mv_rows() returns the predictors' derivative along the directions (and along the block's whitened direction i, when given), one row per observation and per equation, and jfp_jac() returns an equation's Jacobian columns with their positions in the joint vector; the weights Q of jfp_mv_cv() are then on the whitened directions.

Usage

jfp_dir(st, v)

jfp_mv_J(cx, fixed, R)

jfp_mv_e2(cx)

jfp_mv_W(cx, S, eq = cx$a)

jfp_mv_Wk(cx, S, eq = cx$a)

jfp_mv_etak(cx, i, S)

jfp_mv_etakk(cx, i, S, g)

jfp_mv_cv(cx, S, Q, eq = cx$a)

jfp_mv_pfun(pr, A, B)

jfp_nonempty(R)

jfp_mv_setpair(cx, k)

jfp_mv_full(cx, S)

jfp_mv_rows(cx, i, S)

jfp_jac(st, cc)

Arguments

st

A state, from jfp_state().

v

A direction over the joint vector.

cx

A context, from jfp_mv_ctx().

fixed

Equation indices of the derivative in the predictors.

R, S

A character vector naming directions.

eq

The equation of a factor of the block's rows.

i

The position of a moving term among the context's units.

g

Per-observation weights.

Q

Weights over the observations and the block's columns.

pr

A product of two matrices.

A, B

Functions of a set of directions returning a factor.

k

The position of an ordered pair of equations in the context.

cc

An equation.

Value

As described; NULL where a factor is zero.
